title: Six Senses and COMO Uma Paro, 7 nights
price_note: Per person, twin share, Indian nationals: SDF ₹1,200 a night, 4 nights at Six Senses Thimphu and Punakha and 3 at COMO Uma Paro with breakfast and dinner, private car and senior guide, entry fees; flights extra. Other nationals pay USD 100 a night SDF.
meta_description: 7 nights in Bhutan at Six Senses Thimphu and Punakha and COMO Uma Paro: dzongs, Haa over Chele La, Tiger's Nest, spa time. From ₹3,75,000 pp.
summary: A week in western Bhutan built around three of its best hotels: Six Senses on a ridge above Thimphu, Six Senses among Punakha's rice terraces, and three nights at COMO Uma Paro in pine forest above Paro. Private car and senior guide, a day over Chele La to Haa, and time for the spa.
intro: This trip suits travellers who want Bhutan's main sights with room to rest between them. Two nights at Six Senses Thimphu give you the capital from a quiet ridge; two at Six Senses Punakha put you among rice terraces in the warm valley; three at COMO Uma Paro let you hike to Taktsang and cross Chele La, at about 3,988 m the highest road pass in Bhutan, to the Haa valley without changing rooms.

As we understand the current rules, Indian nationals pay a Sustainable Development Fee of ₹1,200 a night and most other nationals USD 100 a night, a rate set to run to 31 August 2027. A licensed guide must accompany you beyond the first checkpoint. These rules have changed often since 2022; check current status before you travel, and we confirm them in writing when you book.
highlights: Six Senses Thimphu on its ridge above the capital
Rice terraces and the dzong from Six Senses Punakha
Three nights at COMO Uma Paro with time for the spa
Chele La at about 3,988 m and the Haa valley temples
The Tiger's Nest with a senior guide at your pace

days.title: Paro to Six Senses Thimphu
days.text: Your guide meets you at Paro airport. Drive along the Paro Chhu to the Chhuzom confluence and up the Wang Chhu to Thimphu, then up to the lodge on its ridge above the city. Lunch and a quiet afternoon to adjust to the altitude of about 2,600 m. Before dinner, watch the lights come on across the valley below.

days.title: Thimphu: chorten, Buddha and dzong
days.text: Begin at the Memorial Chorten, built in 1974 for the third king, then Buddha Dordenma above the city and the Royal Takin Preserve. After lunch, the Institute for Zorig Chusum and, Friday to Sunday, the Centenary Farmers Market. At about 5 pm, Tashichho Dzong as the flag comes down. Evening at the lodge's spa or by the fire.

days.title: Dochu La to Six Senses Punakha
days.text: Stop at Simtokha Dzong, built in 1629, then cross Dochu La at about 3,100 m with its 108 chortens. Descend into the Punakha valley and continue to the lodge among rice terraces above the Mo Chhu. After lunch, walk with your guide through the fields to Chimi Lhakhang, the temple of Drukpa Kunley, built in 1499.

days.title: Punakha Dzong and the valley walk
days.text: Morning at Punakha Dzong, at the confluence of the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu, reached by its covered cantilever bridge. Walk on to the long suspension bridge upstream. In the afternoon, hike up through the terraces to the Khamsum Yulley Namgyal Chorten, about an hour up, or take a gentle float on the Mo Chhu in spring and autumn.

days.title: Punakha to COMO Uma Paro
days.text: Drive back over Dochu La and down to Paro. Check in at COMO Uma Paro, on a hill of pine forest above the town. In the afternoon, cross the covered bridge to Rinpung Dzong and climb to the Ta Dzong watchtower and the National Museum. Then a treatment or a hot stone bath at the spa before dinner.

days.title: Over Chele La to Haa
days.text: Drive up through forest to Chele La at about 3,988 m, the highest road pass in Bhutan, for prayer flags and, on clear mornings, views towards Jomolhari. Walk a short way along the ridge. Descend into the quiet Haa valley to see Lhakhang Karpo and Lhakhang Nagpo, the White and Black temples, and a farmhouse lunch. Return to Paro by late afternoon.

days.title: Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest
days.text: After yesterday's high pass you are ready for the hike. Start early from about 2,600 m and climb through blue pine to the cafeteria viewpoint and the monastery at 3,120 m. Cameras go into lockers at the gate. Back for a late lunch, then Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples, in the evening light.

days.title: Fly out of Paro
days.text: A last breakfast with the view over the Paro valley, then the short transfer to the airport. Flights depend on weather; keep a spare day before onward long-haul connections.

good_to_know: Chele La is about 3,988 m and Taktsang 3,120 m; you sleep no higher than about 2,600 m. Go slowly at height and talk to your doctor before the trip if you have heart or lung conditions.
Sustainable Development Fee: as we understand it, ₹1,200 a night for Indian nationals and USD 100 a night for most others. Check current status before you travel.
Chele La can close after snow from December to March; in that case we reach Haa via Chhuzom or replace the day with a Paro valley walk.
Six Senses and COMO rates vary by season and room type; we confirm in writing when you book.
Dzongs and temples require long sleeves and long trousers or skirts; no photography inside temple rooms.

faqs.q: How much does this luxury Bhutan trip cost?
faqs.a: From about ₹3,75,000 per person, twin share, for Indian nationals, including SDF, hotels with breakfast and dinner, private car and guide. Flights are extra. Non-Indian nationals pay USD 100 a night SDF as we understand it and a visa fee. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Six Senses or Amankora: which should we choose?
faqs.a: Both are among Bhutan's best. Six Senses has larger spas and a more contemporary feel; Amankora lodges are smaller, quieter and share one design. This route mixes Six Senses with COMO Uma Paro. Our Amankora trip covers Gangtey too. Tell us what matters to you and we will advise.

Paro is the base for both Taktsang and the Chele La drive to Haa, and staying put means no packing on hike days. It also puts you 15 minutes from the airport on departure morning, which matters because flights can be delayed or brought forward by weather.

faqs.q: Is the Chele La drive safe?
faqs.a: Yes, with an experienced driver. The road is narrow and steep with hairpin bends, and fog and ice are common in winter. After snow it can close; we then use the longer road via Chhuzom or change the day. Check current status before you travel.

Yes. Six Senses has a lodge at Gangtey overlooking the Phobjikha valley. Adding two nights there between Punakha and Paro brings the black-necked cranes from late October to February. The extra nights add hotel, SDF, guide and car costs.

faqs.q: Is this a good honeymoon trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Short drives, three nights in one place at the end, spa time and quiet hotels make it relaxed. Ask us to request a room with a view at each hotel. March–April and October–November are the best months for weather and flowers or clear skies.

faqs.q: What is included at the spa?
faqs.a: Spa treatments are not included in our price. Six Senses Thimphu has the largest spa of its lodges, and COMO Uma Paro has a COMO Shambhala spa with hot stone bathhouses. Book treatments early in festival seasons, when spa slots fill.

faqs.q: Do Indian nationals need a visa for Bhutan?
faqs.a: No. Indian nationals need a valid passport or voter ID and receive a free entry permit, as we understand the rules. Aadhaar is not accepted. Our licensed partner arranges the permit and route permit before arrival. Check current status before you travel.

Layers: days in Punakha can be 25 °C while nights in Thimphu and Paro fall near freezing in winter. Bring walking shoes for Taktsang, a long-sleeved top and long trousers or skirt for dzongs, sunscreen, a hat and a small daypack.
